title: glTF models and cleanup
cards/0/body: Ready-made models in Three.js are almost always loaded as glTF (.gltf or binary .glb): geometry, PBR materials, textures and animations in one file. The format itself is covered in the "3D formats" course.
cards/1/q: What do you add to the scene after loading?
cards/1/options/0: gltf.scene, a group with all of the model's objects
cards/1/explain: gltf also has animations, cameras and asset; you take those separately.
cards/2/title: The model is huge, or off to one side
cards/2/body: Models arrive at all sorts of scales, with their center anywhere. A bounding box, Box3, helps you put the model in its place.
cards/3/q: Put the steps for showing a model in order
cards/3/items/2: Move it to the center and fit the scale
cards/3/items/4: Set up the lights and the camera
cards/3/explain: Without light, glTF's PBR materials will be black.
cards/4/body: Heavy geometry is compressed with Draco or meshopt, which makes the file several times smaller. The loader needs a decoder:
cards/5/title: Removed from the scene ≠ memory freed
cards/5/body: scene.remove(model) only takes the object out of the scene. Geometry, materials and textures stay in GPU memory until you call dispose(). renderer.info.memory helps you spot a leak.
cards/6/q: A configurator swaps models, and after an hour the tab crashes. renderer.info.memory.geometries keeps growing. What is wrong?
cards/6/options/0: Old models are removed from the scene, but dispose is never called
cards/6/explain: The JavaScript garbage collector does not free GPU memory.
cards/7/explain: current was removed, but its geometry, materials and textures were never freed.
